correctness.rationale: For every sufficiently large odd N, the prime number theorem gives missing odd prime q<=2logN. Minimal a yields base B=2^a q<q^2 and Bq<q^3, with gcd(N,Bq)=1. Binary subset sum certifies each 2^b q (b>=a) Zumkeller. For all primes p<=N/2 in p=N mod B but not in p=N mod Bq, N-p=B m with q not dividing m; after extracting powers of 2 its cofactor is coprime to a higher-power Zumkeller base, proving Zumkeller membership. The count of this subclass equals pi(X;B,N)-pi(X;Bq,N), with X=N/2. Uniform Siegel–Walfisz gives main term Li(X)/phi(B)(1-1/q) since phi(Bq)=q phi(B); its relative error is o(1) uniformly as phi(B)=O(log^2 N) and both moduli are polylogarithmic. Thus R(N)>=the local asymptotic term and R(N)>>N/log^3N. The finite checker separately tests selected exact partitions and congruences; it cannot replace the analytic theorem.

A past fifth-power quantitative result uses a single square-modulus prime class, whereas this theorem counts an entire reduced class and subtracts a single prime-exponent obstruction. Exact divisor-partition multiplicity of 2^a q, the 2^a p q criterion, practical addends, and finite checks are weaker in incompatible or strictly narrower dimensions.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A bound below of order N/(log N)^5 cannot imply a lower bound of order N/(log N)^3. Density-one existence cannot imply this quantitative all-large-target lower bound, and finite-range evidence cannot imply an infinite assertion. The stronger local theorem demands and proves a new exact subtraction identity for prime class mod B and its unique refinement mod Bq; this removes the unnecessary coprimality-to-two restriction and reduces the analytic modulus by a logarithmic factor, while admitting q-1 of q refinements. The published criteria do not state this novel implication. It is not merely a change of numerical constant or rephrasing of the old bound.

value.rationale: Two unbounded logarithmic powers are gained in the guaranteed number of prime-plus-Zumkeller representations for every sufficiently large odd target. The stronger local theorem identifies the exact exceptional q-adic subprogression and shows a fraction 1-1/q of primes in the moving reduced class are explicitly admissible. This is a motivated quantitative refinement of an established open additive question, not a routine constant improvement, substitution or finite census; it does not purport to be an optimal global asymptotic.
